newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Senior Ranariddh party official shot dead.
newsitem.headline: Senior Ranariddh party official shot dead.

text.p: A senior official from ousted Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh's party was shot and killed after being arrested by troops loyal to powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, an interior ministry official said on Tuesday.
Ho Sok, a secretary of state at the Interior Ministry, was arrested on Monday and later killed, Interior Ministry advisor Khieu Sopheak, a member of Hun Sen's party, told reporters.
"He has been arrested by government troops and he died," Khieu Sopheak said. "He was shot down by the people that were angry with him."
Ho Sok, a powerful member of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party, had been involved in "sabotage and plots" Khieu Sopheak said.
He did not say when Ho Sok was killed or who killed him, but said action would be taken for the crime.

Ho Sok was one of four senior FUNCINPEC members who Hun Sen accused of being responsible for two days of fighting in the Cambodian capital that left at least 58 people dead and as many as 200 others, mostly civilians, wounded.
Hun Sen, who unilaterally ousted Ranariddh on Sunday, said that day that the four should be found and arrested.

Ranariddh's top military advisor, General Nhiek Bun Chhay, was among the four identified by Hun Sen. Officials said on Tuesday that Nhiek Bun Chhay was surround by troops loyal to Hun Sen 30 km (18 miles) north of the capital.
The general fled Phnom Penh on Sunday night with Ranariddh loyalists as Hun Sen's forces consolidated their grip on Phnom Penh and its outskirts.
The other two on the list were Chao Sambath, a FUNCINPEC intelligence official, and Serey Kosal, the prince's chief security advisor. Their whereabouts were not immediately known.
